title: Reliable reconstruction and forecasting of single-cell fates

concept.text: The innovation would combine reliable reconstruction of how cell populations developed with prospective forecasts of what those populations will become. Using early molecular measurements, lineage relationships and observations over time, it would estimate which earlier states gave rise to later states and predict the distribution of future cell states, including responses to previously untested perturbations. Its central output would be a set of probabilities with measured uncertainty, rather than a claim to know every individual cell’s destiny.

Reconstruction is indirect because single-cell sequencing often destroys the measured cell. Researchers therefore link measurements from different cells collected at different times, using similarities in molecular state and information about ancestry. Moslin provides a technical basis for this approach by integrating gene expression and lineage information into probabilistic mappings between earlier and later cells. Such mappings can describe plausible histories, but mappings calculated using later observations are retrospective reconstructions; they do not by themselves demonstrate forecasting before those observations exist.

significance.text: If broadly validated, this capability would make explanations of development and disease more directly testable. Competing models of population change could be asked to predict later cell-state distributions, and experiments could distinguish models when their predictions differ. The moslin study illustrates the underlying scientific question in regenerating zebrafish hearts: activated fibroblast states might arise through an intermediate state or emerge independently from a constitutive population. Reliable temporal reconstruction can suggest an answer; independent prospective testing would provide stronger discrimination.

The proposed advance could guide the timing and selection of experiments in development, regeneration and cancer by identifying informative observations and perturbations. Successful forecasts of unseen perturbation responses could help researchers prioritize interventions for experimental testing. The supplied study identifies perturbation prediction as a possible extension and discusses cellular changes in cancer, cardiovascular disease and neurodegenerative disease, but does not demonstrate the proposed forecasting capability in those settings.

Conditional significance assessment: the potentially revolutionary change would be a reproducible ability to anticipate cellular population dynamics across substantially different settings. Accurate forecasts alone would not establish the causal mechanisms producing them, predict an individual patient’s disease course or demonstrate therapeutic control. Those outcomes require additional causal, clinical and intervention evidence. Population-level success would also remain meaningful when individual cells cannot be predicted accurately; the supplied material does not establish a historical ranking of this innovation’s importance.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is reliable prospective generalization: issuing calibrated predictions from information available early, then retaining accuracy when tested against later outcomes and previously untested perturbations. Retrospective temporal linkage is an important foundation, but a model fitted with observations from all available time points has access to information that a genuine forecast would lack. Extending reconstruction to forecasting therefore requires evidence beyond successful mappings of already observed data.

Concrete obstacles include destructive measurements, sparse sampling, incomplete molecular profiles and noisy or incomplete lineage readouts. Distinct histories can remain compatible with the same observations. Rapid convergence or divergence of gene expression can also undermine the assumptions used to connect molecular similarity with ancestry. Lineage information can reduce ambiguity, but imperfect lineage measurements and uncertain state relationships prevent it from resolving every trajectory.

The contribution of unmeasured internal state, environmental signals and biological randomness to individual-fate predictability remains an open question in the supplied evidence. The study discusses using inferred trajectories to investigate internal state versus external signals as a future application; it does not quantify their limits on prediction. Its stochastic sampling model concerns measurement and cannot establish that biological fate decisions are intrinsically stochastic. The engineering challenge is consequently to distinguish uncertainty that better measurements could reduce from uncertainty that persists within a defined forecasting task.

current_state.text: Lange and colleagues’ moslin study, published on October 21, 2024, demonstrated probabilistic temporal mapping by combining lineage tracing and gene expression. Its evaluated settings included simulations, C. elegans embryogenesis and zebrafish heart regeneration. The method uses information from available time points to connect earlier and later cells. These results support retrospective reconstruction in the tested settings; they do not establish the proposed prospective forecasts of later distributions or unseen perturbation responses.

In zebrafish heart regeneration, the authors inferred a possible transition through a col11a1a-expressing fibroblast state toward a col12a1a-expressing state. This addressed competing explanations in which those activated states either form a sequence or arise independently from constitutive fibroblasts. The proposed intermediate relationship remained a hypothesis requiring experimental validation at publication. That qualification concerns the particular inferred transition and should not be generalized into a claim that all fibroblast origins were unvalidated.

The study reported only a small zebrafish performance gain over an expression-only baseline. The supplied review records a 1.2% advantage for nppc fibroblasts in the Results and persistence accuracies of 0.793 for moslin and 0.785 for the comparator denoted W in the Methods. The latter differ by 0.008, equivalent to 0.8 percentage points when expressed as percentages. These comparisons should remain distinct: the supplied material does not establish that the 1.2% figure describes the same metric or whether it denotes a relative improvement or a percentage-point difference.

The available evidence supports this dated account rather than a field-wide assessment as of November 1, 2026. No freshness findings were supplied, and the November 11, 2026 retrieval timestamps do not establish whether subsequent research changed the scientific picture. The supplied review identifies the article and reports that the relevant substantive sections were available, although the retained main-article text was truncated in the references. The source index also records truncated main-paper extractions and supplementary PDF pages without extractable text. The findings summarized here rely on the supplied review’s main-text evidence; they do not imply independent inspection of supplementary figures or inaccessible page content.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: across several developmental and disease systems, use early measurements to preregister forecasts of later cell-state distributions and responses to previously untested perturbations. Specify the available inputs, forecast horizons, target states, perturbations and evaluation rules before revealing outcomes. Later outcomes and validation lineage information should remain outside model fitting and parameter selection. Any lineage measurements legitimately available at forecast time should be distinguished explicitly from information reserved for validation.
completion_criteria.label: Preregistered forecasts predict later states and previously untested perturbation responses

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation: compare forecasts with independent lineage tracing and time-resolved measurements, and prespecify useful accuracy and calibration thresholds for each task. Calibration should test whether predicted probabilities agree with observed frequencies across comparable cases. Compare against simple, prespecified baselines, including expression-only methods where appropriate. Individual-fate comparisons should account for the prevalence of each fate, since predicting the common outcome can outperform a naive equal-chance baseline. Report where predictions fail to improve on these baselines and where uncertainty is too large to distinguish competing outcomes.
completion_criteria.label: Forecasts meet prespecified accuracy and calibration thresholds against independent measurements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: repeat the evaluation in independent biological samples and laboratories, with sufficient access to data, code and analysis choices to reproduce the findings. Report performance separately by system, perturbation, forecast horizon, sampling density and lineage-readout quality, together with experimental and computational requirements. Convincing completion would demonstrate useful, reproducible forecasting within these stated boundaries. These are proposed criteria rather than established standards, and success on a finite collection of systems would demonstrate breadth without proving literal universality or clinical readiness.
completion_criteria.label: Independent samples and laboratories reproduce useful forecasting within reported boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIF-03, “A transferable, predictive virtual cell,” has a broader target of transferable cellular prediction, including perturbation responses. BIF-08 overlaps in predicting how cells change, but could succeed through calibrated population and lineage forecasts without reproducing all cellular mechanisms. Conversely, a broadly predictive virtual cell would still require explicit evidence of reliable fate reconstruction and forecasting to satisfy BIF-08.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-04, “General reconstruction of causal cellular networks,” concerns causal relationships among cellular components. BIF-08 concerns temporal histories and future fate distributions. Temporal ordering, lineage relationships and predictive accuracy can inform causal hypotheses, but do not alone identify the causal network; even successful perturbation forecasts require care before assigning mechanisms.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-07, “Computational reconstruction of organism-scale molecular maps,” could provide spatial and molecular context for fate forecasting. BIF-08 instead centers on change through time and ancestry. A detailed molecular map would not by itself explain where cells came from or forecast their later states, while useful fate forecasts need not reconstruct an entire organism-scale map.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-01, “A predictive decoder for the regulatory genome,” and BIF-13, “Predictive design of functional genetic circuits and pathways,” could help explain or manipulate transitions between cell states. BIF-08 would evaluate the resulting fate distributions and trajectories. Regulatory decoding and circuit design remain distinct achievements: reliable fate prediction need not entail either comprehensive genome interpretation or the ability to design interventions that produce a desired fate.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-10, “A broadly capable autonomous bioinformatics discovery system,” could use fate reconstruction and forecasting as part of an experimental discovery workflow. BIF-08 remains a specific scientific capability that can be evaluated independently of autonomy. Lineage-recording technology is another enabling area: it supplies ancestry evidence, whereas BIF-08 integrates that evidence with molecular state and time to infer histories and test forecasts.

change_log.change: Preserved BIF-08’s identity while defining retrospective reconstruction and prospective population forecasting as distinct capabilities.
change_log.reason: The demonstrated temporal mappings provide a foundation but do not establish forecasts issued before later observations become available.

change_log.change: Integrated destructive measurement, sparse sampling, incomplete molecular measurements, imperfect lineage readouts and expression convergence or divergence into the explanation of barriers.
change_log.reason: These are concrete sources of ambiguity documented in the supplied review and explain why lineage information does not resolve every history.

change_log.change: Qualified claims about environmental effects and stochastic biological fate decisions.
change_log.reason: The supplied study discusses environmental analysis as a future application, and stochastic measurement sampling does not prove intrinsic randomness in biological fate.

change_log.change: Dated the demonstrated results to October 21, 2024 and preserved the limits of the freshness and extraction record.
change_log.reason: Retrieval dates do not establish scientific currency, and the supplied evidence does not support a field-wide assessment as of November 1, 2026 or imply inspection of all supplementary content.

change_log.change: Specified the unvalidated fibroblast intermediate hypothesis and retained the small zebrafish baseline advantage with its reported numerical comparisons.
change_log.reason: The qualification applies to a particular inferred transition. The 1.2% figure and the 0.793 versus 0.785 persistence accuracies should not be conflated.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria to address information leakage, prespecified horizons and thresholds, calibration, prevalence-aware baselines and independent reproduction.
change_log.reason: These additions make the proposed advance assessable while distinguishing proposed evaluation rules from established standards.

change_log.change: Integrated conditional significance and roster distinctions without merging concepts.
change_log.reason: Fate forecasting could guide experiments, but causal identification, patient prognosis, therapeutic control, virtual-cell modeling and autonomous discovery require distinct evidence.

unresolved_issues: Whether subsequent work changed the state of reconstruction or prospective fate forecasting by November 1, 2026 remains unresolved because no freshness findings were supplied.
The supplied evidence does not quantify how much individual-fate uncertainty arises from unmeasured internal state, environmental influences or intrinsic biological randomness.
The inferred transition through the col11a1a-expressing fibroblast state required experimental validation at the 2024 publication; its subsequent validation status is unknown here.
The precise metric and relative-versus-percentage-point interpretation of the reported 1.2% nppc fibroblast advantage cannot be resolved from the supplied summary.

Forecast horizons, application-specific accuracy and calibration thresholds, required system coverage and practical resource limits remain to be specified before implementing the proposed demonstration.
The supplied review supports the main-text conclusions summarized here but does not establish a complete assessment of supplementary figure content affected by extraction limitations.

brief.title: Reconstructing and predicting how cells change
possible: Researchers could trace how a population of cells developed and predict what it will become from early measurements. The predictions would give the chances of different outcomes, with measured uncertainty, rather than promise to know every cell’s destiny.
They could also forecast how cells respond to experimental changes that have never been tested, helping them choose which experiments to run next.
why: This would make explanations of development, tissue repair and disease easier to test. Researchers could compare competing explanations by asking each to predict later outcomes, then see which matches what happens.
For researchers studying regeneration and cancer, useful forecasts could guide when to measure cells and which possible interventions deserve experimental testing.

sources.showed: Their moslin method combined gene expression—which genes are active—with cell ancestry to estimate links between earlier and later cells. They tested it in simulations, worm development and zebrafish heart repair.
sources.quote: Our approach outperforms LineageOT, CoSpar, and OT-baselines on simulated data where ground truth is available.
sources.cited_for: Combining molecular measurements with ancestry can help reconstruct how cell populations changed.
sources.not_established: Links calculated using later observations do not establish forecasts made before those observations exist.

sources.who: Grace Hui Ting Yeo, Sachit D. Saksena and David K. Gifford
sources.showed: Their PRESCIENT model predicted the chances of blood cells reaching different outcomes when it accounted for cell multiplication. Simulations also recovered expected effects of known genes controlling cell development.
sources.quote:
We show that when accounting for cell
proliferation, PRESCIENT outperforms existing methods on
predicting cell fate bias.
sources.cited_for: Models can predict some cell outcomes and simulate responses to changes in gene activity.
sources.not_established: Recovering known effects does not establish reliable forecasts of previously untested experimental changes.

shown: Lange and colleagues demonstrated reconstruction across several biological settings. Yeo and colleagues demonstrated some outcome prediction and simulated interventions. Together, these results provide parts of the capability; neither demonstrates the full combination of reliable reconstruction and advance forecasting.
missing: Forecasts made from early information still need to succeed on later outcomes and previously untested experimental changes.
Predicted probabilities still need to match observed frequencies and beat simple comparisons on independent measurements.
Independent laboratories still need to reproduce useful forecasting and establish where it works.

milestones.label: Advance forecasts succeed across development and disease
milestones.explanation: Forecasts of later cell populations and untested experimental changes would have to be registered before outcomes are revealed, using only early inputs. This would establish prediction across several systems without access to later answers.

milestones.label: Accuracy and probabilities pass independent tests
milestones.explanation: Independent measurements would have to confirm preset accuracy targets, probabilities matching observed frequencies, and gains over simple comparisons. This would establish whether forecasts provide useful, trustworthy information.

milestones.label: Independent laboratories reproduce useful forecasts within stated limits
milestones.explanation: Independent samples and laboratories would have to reproduce useful forecasts with enough shared detail to repeat the work and with performance limits reported. This would establish reliability across the conditions tested.

uncertain: How much uncertainty comes from missing measurements, environmental signals or biological randomness remains unknown.
Useful forecast lengths, accuracy targets and acceptable experimental and computing costs remain to be defined.

page.title: Single-cell fate reconstruction and forecasting
page.definition: A model reconstructs cell ancestry and predicts later distributions of cell states from earlier molecular measurements, including responses to interventions absent from training. Its fate probabilities—chances of reaching specified cell states—agree with independently observed outcome frequencies.

goal.need: In the mouse blood-cell benchmark below, improved fate discrimination remained below a clonal-data reference. Training used days 2, 4 and 6, so these results leave forecasting before later observations, and responses to untested interventions, as separate experimental goals.

figures.caption: Fate discrimination in the published mouse blood-cell benchmark.
figures.note: AUROC is area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; it measures discrimination, not calibration. PRESCIENT summarizes five random seeds.

completion.title: One model passes independent prospective tests of ancestry reconstruction and calibrated fate forecasts.
completion.criterion: In one specified biological system, a single model reconstructs ancestry against independent lineage measurements and, using only information available at forecast time, predicts later fate distributions with and without an intervention absent from training. An independent laboratory confirms improvement over expression-only and no-change baselines and probability calibration against newly measured outcomes. The forecast horizon, scoring rules and calibration acceptance criteria are fixed before outcomes are collected. This is a provisional capability test; no universal numerical cutoff is established.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; provisional test because no external endpoint covering the combined capability was found.
completion.basis: CZI and Arc goals, Cellular Intelligence’s roadmap, and lineage/fate and Virtual Embryo benchmarks were searched for a joint prospective reconstruction, perturbation and calibration endpoint; none was found. The provisional test limits the claim to one biological system and requires independent experimental validation. The published benchmarks below establish separate components.

milestones.title: A model reconstructs worm ancestry across seven time bins with lower error than competing mappings.
milestones.criterion: Use 6,476 C. elegans ABpxp cells in seven time bins spanning 170–510 minutes after fertilization. Fit cross-time mappings using expression and within-time lineage distances; evaluate against the published cross-time ancestry annotations using mean ancestor/descendant error. Obtain lower error than LineageOT and expression-only transport for every evaluated time-point pair. Moslin reported this result on 21 October 2024; it is retrospective reconstruction.
milestones.set_by: Lange et al., published C. elegans comparative benchmark in the moslin paper; a study-specific test rather than a field-wide acceptance cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: For all time point pairs, moslin outperforms other methods and achieves a lower mean error

milestones.title: A model outperforms Waddington-OT and FateID on the published clonal-fate benchmark.
milestones.criterion: Predict day-6 neutrophil bias for 335 day-2 mouse progenitors: neutrophils divided by neutrophils plus monocytes. Beat Waddington-OT and FateID on both Pearson correlation and discrimination of bias greater than 0.5, using the published test set. PRESCIENT reported this comparison on 28 May 2021; its discrimination score appears above.
milestones.set_by: Yeo et al., PRESCIENT Figure 2 comparison using the Weinreb clonal-fate benchmark; a study-specific comparative test.
milestones.threshold_quote: We show that when accounting for cell proliferation, PRESCIENT outperforms existing methods on predicting cell fate bias.

milestones.title: A model predicts a new fate shift confirmed by two experimental perturbations.
milestones.criterion: Predict increased prechordal-plate differentiation after loss of noto, then confirm that direction in both mutant and CRISPR-disrupted zebrafish embryos at 10 hours after fertilization. CellOracle reported this on 8 February 2023. Mutant samples pooled 25 embryos, with two biological replicates per condition; the prechordal-plate fraction increased 38.6% relative to controls (chi-square P = 1.07 × 10⁻⁴). CRISPR disruption provided a second experimental validation.
milestones.set_by: Kamimoto et al., CellOracle experimental validation in Figures 3–4; this test concerns zebrafish noto loss of function specifically.
milestones.threshold_quote: Next, we experimentally validated the predicted expansion of prechordal plate after noto LOF.

milestones.title: One architecture exceeds 150 points across the three Virtual Embryo Challenge tasks.
milestones.criterion: Use one shared architecture across all three Virtual Embryo Challenge tasks and obtain a final hidden-test total above 150 out of 300. Tasks cover future expression distributions, spatial-temporal prediction and an unseen knockout. Scores average each task’s boards and sum the three task scores; the floor scores 50 per task. Separate training and prediction heads are allowed. This combines the organisers’ prize-eligibility floor with their shared-architecture condition; it does not establish calibration or ancestry reconstruction.
milestones.set_by: Qiu Lab at Stanford University and collaborators, Virtual Embryo Challenge 2026 Official Rules, sections 13–14; shared architecture is the Generality Award condition.
milestones.threshold_quote: The floor is published on every board and scores 50 there by construction, so a team entering all three tasks must total more than 150.

not_found: Cellular Intelligence’s roadmap specifies 80% and 90% accuracy targets without defining the accuracy metric or a fixed evaluation population.
Virtual Embryo Challenge team scores were not exposed in the accessible leaderboard page on 14 November 2026.
The publisher-hosted PRESCIENT PDF was inaccessible; its PMC PDF mirror was accessible.

results.finding: Moslin reconstructed ancestry for 6,476 C. elegans ABpxp cells with lower mean error than competing methods across all evaluated time-point pairs.
results.detail: The retrospective analysis used seven time points spanning 170–510 minutes after fertilization and evaluated mappings against published lineage annotations. Comparators included LineageOT and expression-only transport.
results.quote: For all time point pairs, moslin outperforms other methods and achieves a lower mean error

results.finding: PRESCIENT predicted clonal fate bias for 335 mouse progenitors, achieving AUROC 0.725.
results.detail: With expression-derived proliferation estimates, Pearson r was 0.399. Waddington-OT scored r = 0.150 and AUROC = 0.599; FateID scored r = 0.225 and AUROC = 0.602. Models were trained on all three time points.
results.quote:
We found

achieved r = 0.399 ± 0.025 and AUROC = 0.725 ± 0.008, a slight
improvement over empirical proliferation rate based models
(Fig. 2f, g).

results.finding: In noto-loss zebrafish embryos, pooled samples of 25 mutants showed a 38.6% increase in the prechordal-plate fraction.
results.detail: CellOracle predicted enhanced prechordal-plate differentiation. At 10 hours post-fertilization, both mutants and CRISPR-disrupted embryos showed expansion. Mutant and control samples had two biological replicates each; the mutant chi-square P value was 1.07 × 10⁻⁴.
